articles.title: La semana de fichajes que marcará todo
articles.standfirst: 'En Copa de Balón', una opinión de Elías Israel
articles.summary: 'En Copa de Balón', una opinión de Elías Israel
articles.body: Pregúntenle a cualquier entrenador de Primera cuál es la semana más importante de su temporada y ninguno les señalará un derbi. Les señalará ésta. La que empieza hoy. Porque un partido se pierde y se recupera, pero una plantilla mal cerrada no se recupera, se arrastra. No hay discurso, ni pizarra, ni sesión de vídeo que corrija a un vestuario corto. Los directores deportivos llevan todo el verano trabajando para esta semana, porque es cuando el mercado por fin se ablanda. No hay magia. Hay meses de llamadas para estar en el sitio exacto el día correcto. En el primer escalón pelean los juegan a otra cosa: El Barça sigue pendiente de su Plan A, que es tan sencillo de enunciar como difícil de resolver: un delantero titular. Uno que garantice los goles de Lewandowski y Ferran Torres. La exhibición de Elche puede ser impostora. Si se quiere pelear por la Champions, ésa figura es clave. El Madrid, en cambio, tiene plan B. Se llama Espí y le da una respuesta arriba. Su problema está en el medio. Necesita imperiosamente al centrocampista que le permita dominar el juego, ese Rodri que no llegó. En el segundo escalón, el Atlético dirime estos días su plan J. J de Julián. El desapego del Metropolitano con ‘La Araña’ ha dejado de ser una pitada memorable para convertirse en una decisión difícil. Julián está mustio, desorientado por sus agentes, y ese estado anímico invita a pensar en una gran venta a la Premier necesaria. En el tercer escalón, solo hay un objetivo: sobrevivir como se pueda. Monchi intenta hacer su magia de siempre con Bryan Zaragoza, que es su manera de recordar que el ingenio todavía cotiza. Toni Muñoz reinventa el Getafe a un coste irrisorio, un ejercicio que en cualquier otra Liga tendría nombre de escuela de negocios. Las penalidades reales de la competición se vieron con crudeza en el Osasuna-Levante: dos clubes que han ingresado una cantidad muy considerable por Víctor Muñoz y Carlos Espí, respectivamente, y que no reinvierten ni una quinta parte de lo cobrado. Eso también es la Liga. Valencia y Sevilla gestionan sus miserias dirigenciales de la mejor manera posible, que es un elogio triste. El Betis necesita acelerar, porque su mercado no va en absoluto acorde con las ilusiones que genera. Y la Real Sociedad lo ha dejado todo para el final, con todo lo que eso conlleva. Me salen hasta diez equipos que se agarran a lo que hay y solo sueñan con que haya tres equipos peores. Es un objetivo modesto, pero es el objetivo real de demasiados. La semana decisiva de otro mercado recesivo. Salvo para los grandes, que un año más juegan en otra Liga.

articles.title: Jose Mourinho 'calmer' as he enjoys Real Madrid return
articles.summary: Jose Mourinho claims to be a much cooler character as he prepares for his first home game in charge of Real Madrid since 2013 against Real Sociedad on Wednes...
articles.body:
Jose Mourinho claims to be a much cooler character as he prepares for his first home game in charge of Real Madrid since 2013 against Real Sociedad on Wednesday night.

But the 63-year-old conceded his relaxed demeanour might not last if his latest group of Galacticos fail to bridge the eight-point gap that saw them finish second in last season's LaLiga behind rivals Barcelona .

Mourinho began his latest spell in charge with a hard-fought 2-1 win over Espanyol at the weekend and believes he has seen enough to keep his notorious temper at bay for the time being.

"For years now I've felt calmer, with more control over my emotions," said Mourinho, whose first spell had its most controversial moment when he poked then-Barcelona coach Tito Vilanova in the eye after a Spanish Super Cup tie in 2011.

"But we will have to face difficult and frustrating situations that will come, which haven't come yet because we won the first match and I haven't seen anyone slacking off yet.

"I like that people work for Real Madrid, not just at Real Madrid. So far, I haven't felt any laziness, I've seen that everyone wants to give their best.

"Maybe it's the players and the people who work here who are protecting me from the darker side of my personality. But I feel good this way."

Mourinho was in a magnanimous mood after the opening game, praising his opponents and even the referee, and was at pains to play down the importance of his own personal reappearance on the touchline at the Bernabeu.

"I don't want the Bernabeu to welcome me in a particular way, I want it to welcome the team as its team and its passion," Mourinho added.

"I think people have already got a feeling for the way the team is working, its commitment, and the will to do things right. That's the most important thing - I'm not important.

"At the Bernabeu, we hope for the support of our people. What I expect is for the players to have the same hunger to win the match, the same attitude, resilience, strength and calmness to face a difficult game.

"I hope the fans can look at the team and recognise this kind of mentality, and maybe this kind of mentality can make the Bernabeu even stronger."

Aurelien Tchouameni has dropped out of the Real Madrid squad for the match, while Mourinho has indicated his desire to act sparingly with the likes of Jude Bellingham who returned for pre-season having undergone lengthy World Cup campaigns.

Sociedad, who opened their new campaign with a 1-0 defeat to Real Betis on Friday, have named Goncalo Guedes in their squad for the first time since he was forced to pull out of Portugal's World Cup squad due to injury.

articles.title: Olivia Smith: Â£1m Arsenal striker wins second straight PFA young player award
articles.summary: Olivia Smith's career has been in the limelight since she was 15 - but she had been preparing herself for it even before she was a professional footballer.
articles.body:
Olivia Smith has lived her life under a spotlight since she was 15 - but she had been preparing herself even before she became a professional footballer.

Now 22, Smith became the first Â£1m women's footballer last year when Arsenal signed her in a world record deal from Liverpool.

She had joined Liverpool for a club record of Â£210,000 just one season earlier, having made a name for herself when she was given her Canada debut aged 15.

Smith became the first woman to score for Liverpool at Anfield in a Women's Super League match in October 2025.

Now, for the second year in a row, she is the first non-English recipient of the PFA women's young player of the year award.

But how did Smith's sacrifices early in life help her reach the top?

Humble & sweet, but a lion - the story of the first female Â£1m player Published 6 September 2025

Humble & sweet, but a lion - the story of the first female Â£1m player

Find interviews and extra content on the BBC Women's Football Weekly feed

Splits, planks, South American and Jamaican flair

Smith grew up in the small Canadian city of Whitby, where from a young age she was encouraged to play football by her father, Sean.

She jumped between local clubs every year and played with boys until the age of 12 before finally settling into a girls' team.

Clearly talented, she continued to train with boys at the same time, while enjoying a multi-cultural upbringing around Toronto.

"My parents have made a lot of sacrifices taking me to all these places and moving every couple of years," Smith told BBC Sport.

"My dad's Jamaican, my mom's Chilean and Peruvian. There's so much football culture within those.

"I grasped a lot of that from my dad's dad who played football and my mom's dad also played in South America. I think I have that flair in my DNA.

"Of course, I [enjoy the different] food, music, all those kinds of things. In Toronto, you find it is a very multicultural place and that was really cool growing up."

But Smith later experienced bullying and turned to different sports as coping mechanisms, not knowing at the time how it would help her football career.

"I did taekwondo as a kid. I was getting bullied in school so it was more of a defensive mechanism kind of thing," said Smith.

"I did gymnastics too. That really helps with my agility. I find that, for my stature, I'm quite flexible as well, which really helps injury prevention.

"Taekwondo really helped with my discipline and arguably my shooting ability in terms of its speed.

"I think mainly it was just to keep me active, out of trouble, and it was just for fun. Thankfully it contributed to my footballing career."

Smith also thinks the unusual sporting background helped her when dealing with attention and pressure, as well as bullying.

"It helps with just the discipline on and off the pitch in simple tasks that are really important in my day-to-day life," added Smith.

"In gymnastics, you have to do splits or planks for [a length of time]. It's really hard mentally so that helped me mature. I developed a lot of mental toughness."

Dad's goals diary, Smith's Ballon d'Or dreams

It is not just Smith who has invested in football since a young age. Her dad, Sean, was tracking her statistics to monitor her progress.

"That is his favourite thing in the world to do. When I was younger, he would literally film all my games," said Smith.

"After games, we would go back and watch everything, see what I could have done better and what I did well.

"He kept a diary of the goals that I scored, what minute it was in and things like that. He still has it to this day. He loves it!"

Beyond football, Smith loves to cook and watch TV series - Law and Order: SVU is a current favourite - and she says she is "dying to get a puppy".

The young forward has learned to become independent, having left home as a teenager in order to chase a professional career.

But it hasn't been easy. When Smith moved to Michigan aged 15 on her own, she didn't know where she would be living when she boarded the plane.

"Moving around a lot, you're sacrificing relationships because you make good friends in one place, then you have to move," said Smith.

"That makes it quite tough, especially when you're young. I struggled a lot with that. I had to leave to get training elsewhere.

"It helped me get used to what was to come, so I think it was a very important sacrifice in my journey.

"I'm so grateful that I've been able to make so many connections in different places, so even though I'm away from home I feel like I have family."

For the first time in her career, Smith is about to begin a second season at the same club having settled into life at Arsenal.

"When I stepped into the building for my second pre-season it just felt surreal. It feels like home. It feels like Arsenal's the place that's meant to be," said Smith.

"It's an honour to be here. I'm just super excited to see where it takes me. I've always wanted to be somewhere for more than a year; I've moved around so much.

"I also knew there was so much more for me and I wanted to be the best that I could be. All those moves led me here."

At the age of six or seven, she wrote down in a journal what she wanted to achieve.

"I had a journal with everything in it that I wanted to accomplish and what I wanted to do: I want to win the Ballon d'Or. I want to win the World Cup," she added.

"That's still the case today. I want to win trophies with [Arsenal]. I've had this mentality since I was young. It is what has driven me this far."

articles.title: Joao Pedro: Is Brazilian ready to break Chelsea's so-called number nine curse?
articles.summary: Joao Pedro took just 31 seconds to score his opening goal of the season - will the new number nine reach the 20 he scored last season while wearing the number 20 shirt?
articles.body:
Joao Pedro took just 31 seconds to make a statement about how he is handling the so-called curse of the number nine shirt at Chelsea .

The Brazilian deftly lifted his shot over Fulham goalkeeper Bernd Leno to set his side on their way to a dramatic 3-2 win at Craven Cottage in manager Xabi Alonso's first game in charge on Monday.

It was a memorable weekend for Joao Pedro personally, having been handed the coveted number nine shirt and improved financial terms on a new contract that will run until 2034.

It might seem trite, but there is a sizeable group of Chelsea supporters who believe in the so-called curse.

Not since Dutch striker Jimmy Floyd Hasselbaink left the club in 2004 have the club had a prolific striker in the number nine shirt.

Didier Drogba wore number 11 during his successful spell at Stamford Bridge and Diego Costa had the number 19 shirt, but high-profile forwards including Romelu Lukaku, Alvaro Morata, Gonzalo Higuain, Radamel Falcao and Pierre-Emerick Aubameyang struggled while wearing number nine.

All endured difficult and relatively short periods at the club.

The last player to wear the shirt before Joao Pedro was Liam Delap, who is currently in talks with Nottingham Forest about leaving Stamford Bridge after scoring only one Premier League goal last season.

Non-strikers, including midfielder Steve Sidwell and defender Khalid Boulahrouz, also wore the shirt, although some supporters would argue Tammy Abraham performed well as the number nine before his move to Roma.

Asked about the curse after scoring against Fulham , while starring alongside both Cole Palmer and club-record Â£117m signing Morgan Rogers, Joao Pedro told the Mirror: "I don't believe in that. I don't think numbers can decide this pressure."

Last season, the 24-year-old matched his shirt number by scoring 20 goals in all competitions, becoming the first Chelsea striker since Diego Costa to reach that mark nine years earlier.

It has left the Blues delighted with the Â£55m deal, plus up to Â£5m in add-ons, they agreed with Brighton to sign the forward last summer. Those close to Joao Pedro also believe his recent recognition is justified.

In addition, his close-knit entourage have no concerns about his ability to handle the pressure of being Chelsea 's leading man, having shared in his remarkable rise to the top.

Three reasons Chelsea could challenge for title - and one they may not Published 1 day ago

Three reasons Chelsea could challenge for title - and one they may not

Building resilience & physical strength after struggles

"If I gave him one thing, it is to fight for what you want all the time," his mother Flavia Junqueira explained to BBC Sport.

Looking at Joao Pedro's story, that is exactly what he has had to do.

His mother, along with his grandmother, have largely brought him up.

Reports from Joao Pedro's early childhood show his father, former Botafogo footballer Jose Joao de Jesus - more commonly known as Chicao - spent around eight years in prison after being charged as an accessory to murder and was rarely around.

Junqueira later separated from him and focused on her son's footballing potential.

"Joao had a dream," she said. "I shared that dream with my son. The dream didn't have a price."

Growing up in Ribeirao Preto, a nine-hour drive inland from Rio de Janeiro, Joao Pedro was eventually scouted by one of the city's clubs Fluminense, along with a host of other leading Brazilian clubs.

Fluminense were regarded as the best option for the youngster's development, who, like his father, began as a defensive midfielder before progressing further forward.

That choice was, however, fraught with difficulty.

Junqueira left her job, friends and family for Rio, and Joao Pedro "cried a lot" during the journey and in the weeks that followed because of homesickness.

Even in the academy, he was told he "wasn't strong enough" and would not make it. Again, it made him cry.

But his mother, despite her increasingly limited means after leaving her job, hired a personal trainer for her son.

At first, he ate well and trained well only because she told him to. Eventually, however, the penny dropped.

"He was very skinny and there was a significant physical disparity between him and the other athletes in his age group," his long-time personal trainer Rodrigo Goncalves told BBC Sport.

"He never stopped training. Sometimes he went a bit reluctantly, pushed by his mother, but he went.

"Over the years, however, that changed. He began to mature and understand that training wasn't just something his mother required, but rather a tool to improve his performance, develop his body and build the physical balance needed for football."

Joao Pedro became one of the stars of Fluminense's academy and was spotted by Watford's South America scout Rafa Monfort. A phone call from now- Tottenham striker Richarlison, who had made the same move, also proved crucial.

As a child, Joao Pedro was hooked on Premier League football, so the idea of moving to Watford appealed to him. However, it took around eight months to meet the Governing Body Endorsement criteria and secure a UK work permit.

Junqueira believes an overhead kick scored by Joao Pedro, then 17, against Cruzeiro in May 2019 helped convince decision-makers he was an exceptional talent worthy of the move.

When the family arrived in December 2019, Junqueira had not anticipated her bank cards would not work in England. However, then-Watford goalkeeper Heurelho Gomes, also Brazilian, took them under his wing and even bought them Christmas dinner.

A few months later, Covid and lockdown arrived, but Joao Pedro used the unprecedented period to focus on physical training with Goncalves again. He transformed his body by gaining around eight kilograms of body mass and became Premier League-ready.

After that period, he was no longer the little boy who cried, but a fully-fledged top-flight star capable of taking each step and challenge in his stride.

Joao Pedro extends Chelsea stay until 2034 Published 3 days ago

Joao Pedro extends Chelsea stay until 2034

Delap loses number nine shirt & trains away from first team Published 6 days ago

Delap loses number nine shirt & trains away from first team

'When he's angry, he doesn't shout, but goes quiet'

After a deal was agreed with Brighton last summer, Joao Pedro left a training camp in Rio de Janeiro under the guidance of Goncalves to join the Chelsea squad in Miami and immediately take part in the Fifa Club World Cup.

Remarkably, he scored twice in the semi-final against former club Fluminense - just days after arriving at the club. He was also on target in a sensational 3-0 win over Paris St-Germain in the final, widely regarded as Chelsea 's best moment under their current American ownership.

The Blues endured a dismal campaign following that triumph, finishing 10th in the Premier League and ending the season without a trophy and failing to qualify for Europe.

Despite that, Joao Pedro won Chelsea 's player of the season award and is among a group of senior players convinced the project can succeed under Alonso.

Like midfielder Moises Caicedo and captain Reece James, he signed a new contract, while Palmer has also outlined his commitment to stay amid links with Manchester United .

All four are viewed as key culture-setters at the club.

Joao Pedro, in particular, impressed staff by giving more interviews than any other player during a season in which there were few positives to discuss.

Multiple sources have previously told BBC Sport Chelsea have a dressing-room culture problem, specifically with cliques forming along language lines.

Joao Pedro and Palmer, who count each other among their closest friends, are viewed as two of the players capable of naturally bridging those divides.

It helps that Joao Pedro has his family in the UK and has embraced aspects of local culture, having first developed an interest through his love of the Premier League. He is known to listen to trap music, a UK form of hip-hop, and both he and Palmer appeared in pop icon Madonna's promotional short film Confessions II in June.

One of Alonso's main objectives is to rebuild a wayward culture which some sources have described to BBC Sport as overly "transactional" and "cold".

After his front three, including debutant Rogers, scored against Fulham , Alonso said: "They need to take responsibility. They need to lead the rest. They need to inspire the rest because if they do great, the others will follow."

Few know how Joao Pedro handled his omission from the Brazil squad at the World Cup, where they were knocked out in the last 16 by Norway this summer.

Even those closest to him do not know how disappointed he was to miss out, given that playing for Brazil at a World Cup had long been one of his biggest dreams.

"When Joao Pedro is angry, he doesn't shout, he goes quiet," Junqueira said of his general personality.

After Chelsea 's struggles season and the lack of World Cup involvement, he had two weeks completely off.

Joao Pedro spent the rest of his summer in Rio training with Goncalves, his personal fitness coach since childhood, surrounded by friends and following many of the same routines he always has.

Ultimately, according to Goncalves, the frontman remains the same person, but one intent on becoming a truly "elite".

Since returning to Chelsea in the summer, he has scored eight goals in seven pre-season matches before finding the net 31 seconds into the new campaign at Fulham .

It now appears Joao Pedro may be the one capable of finally ending talk and concern of the club's number nine curse.

It was a memorable weekend for Joao Pedro personally, having been handed the coveted number nine shirt and improved financial terms on a new contract that will run until 2034.
It might seem trite, but there is a sizeable group of Chelsea supporters who believe in the so-called curse.
Not since Dutch striker Jimmy Floyd Hasselbaink left the club in 2004 have the club had a prolific striker in the number nine shirt.

Didier Drogba wore number 11 during his successful spell at Stamford Bridge and Diego Costa had the number 19 shirt, but high-profile forwards including Romelu Lukaku, Alvaro Morata, Gonzalo Higuain, Radamel Falcao and Pierre-Emerick Aubameyang struggled while wearing number nine.
All endured difficult and relatively short periods at the club.

The last player to wear the shirt before Joao Pedro was Liam Delap, who is currently in talks with Nottingham Forest about leaving Stamford Bridge after scoring only one Premier League goal last season.

Non-strikers, including midfielder Steve Sidwell and defender Khalid Boulahrouz, also wore the shirt, although some supporters would argue Tammy Abraham performed well as the number nine before his move to Roma.

Asked about the curse after scoring against Fulham , while starring alongside both Cole Palmer and club-record Â£117m signing Morgan Rogers, Joao Pedro told the Mirror: "I don't believe in that. I don't think numbers can decide this pressure."
Last season, the 24-year-old matched his shirt number by scoring 20 goals in all competitions, becoming the first Chelsea striker since Diego Costa to reach that mark nine years earlier.

It has left the Blues delighted with the Â£55m deal, plus up to Â£5m in add-ons, they agreed with Brighton to sign the forward last summer. Those close to Joao Pedro also believe his recent recognition is justified.
In addition, his close-knit entourage have no concerns about his ability to handle the pressure of being Chelsea 's leading man, having shared in his remarkable rise to the top.

Three reasons Chelsea could challenge for title - and one they may not
Building resilience & physical strength after struggles
"If I gave him one thing, it is to fight for what you want all the time," his mother Flavia Junqueira explained to BBC Sport.
Looking at Joao Pedro's story, that is exactly what he has had to do.
His mother, along with his grandmother, have largely brought him up.

Reports from Joao Pedro's early childhood show his father, former Botafogo footballer Jose Joao de Jesus - more commonly known as Chicao - spent around eight years in prison after being charged as an accessory to murder and was rarely around.
Junqueira later separated from him and focused on her son's footballing potential.
"Joao had a dream," she said. "I shared that dream with my son. The dream didn't have a price."

Growing up in Ribeirao Preto, a nine-hour drive inland from Rio de Janeiro, Joao Pedro was eventually scouted by one of the city's clubs Fluminense, along with a host of other leading Brazilian clubs.
Fluminense were regarded as the best option for the youngster's development, who, like his father, began as a defensive midfielder before progressing further forward.
That choice was, however, fraught with difficulty.
Junqueira left her job, friends and family for Rio, and Joao Pedro "cried a lot" during the journey and in the weeks that followed because of homesickness.
Even in the academy, he was told he "wasn't strong enough" and would not make it. Again, it made him cry.
But his mother, despite her increasingly limited means after leaving her job, hired a personal trainer for her son.
At first, he ate well and trained well only because she told him to. Eventually, however, the penny dropped.
"He was very skinny and there was a significant physical disparity between him and the other athletes in his age group," his long-time personal trainer Rodrigo Goncalves told BBC Sport.
"He never stopped training. Sometimes he went a bit reluctantly, pushed by his mother, but he went.

"Over the years, however, that changed. He began to mature and understand that training wasn't just something his mother required, but rather a tool to improve his performance, develop his body and build the physical balance needed for football."

Joao Pedro became one of the stars of Fluminense's academy and was spotted by Watford's South America scout Rafa Monfort. A phone call from now- Tottenham striker Richarlison, who had made the same move, also proved crucial.

As a child, Joao Pedro was hooked on Premier League football, so the idea of moving to Watford appealed to him. However, it took around eight months to meet the Governing Body Endorsement criteria and secure a UK work permit.
Junqueira believes an overhead kick scored by Joao Pedro, then 17, against Cruzeiro in May 2019 helped convince decision-makers he was an exceptional talent worthy of the move.

When the family arrived in December 2019, Junqueira had not anticipated her bank cards would not work in England. However, then-Watford goalkeeper Heurelho Gomes, also Brazilian, took them under his wing and even bought them Christmas dinner.

A few months later, Covid and lockdown arrived, but Joao Pedro used the unprecedented period to focus on physical training with Goncalves again. He transformed his body by gaining around eight kilograms of body mass and became Premier League-ready.
After that period, he was no longer the little boy who cried, but a fully-fledged top-flight star capable of taking each step and challenge in his stride.

Joao Pedro extends Chelsea stay until 2034
Delap loses number nine shirt & trains away from first team Published 6 days ago
Delap loses number nine shirt & trains away from first team
'When he's angry, he doesn't shout, but goes quiet'

After a deal was agreed with Brighton last summer, Joao Pedro left a training camp in Rio de Janeiro under the guidance of Goncalves to join the Chelsea squad in Miami and immediately take part in the Fifa Club World Cup.

Remarkably, he scored twice in the semi-final against former club Fluminense - just days after arriving at the club. He was also on target in a sensational 3-0 win over Paris St-Germain in the final, widely regarded as Chelsea 's best moment under their current American ownership.
The Blues endured a dismal campaign following that triumph, finishing 10th in the Premier League and ending the season without a trophy and failing to qualify for Europe.
Despite that, Joao Pedro won Chelsea 's player of the season award and is among a group of senior players convinced the project can succeed under Alonso.
Like midfielder Moises Caicedo and captain Reece James, he signed a new contract, while Palmer has also outlined his commitment to stay amid links with Manchester United .
All four are viewed as key culture-setters at the club.
Joao Pedro, in particular, impressed staff by giving more interviews than any other player during a season in which there were few positives to discuss.
Multiple sources have previously told BBC Sport Chelsea have a dressing-room culture problem, specifically with cliques forming along language lines.
Joao Pedro and Palmer, who count each other among their closest friends, are viewed as two of the players capable of naturally bridging those divides.

It helps that Joao Pedro has his family in the UK and has embraced aspects of local culture, having first developed an interest through his love of the Premier League. He is known to listen to trap music, a UK form of hip-hop, and both he and Palmer appeared in pop icon Madonna's promotional short film Confessions II in June.
One of Alonso's main objectives is to rebuild a wayward culture which some sources have described to BBC Sport as overly "transactional" and "cold".

After his front three, including debutant Rogers, scored against Fulham , Alonso said: "They need to take responsibility. They need to lead the rest. They need to inspire the rest because if they do great, the others will follow."
Few know how Joao Pedro handled his omission from the Brazil squad at the World Cup, where they were knocked out in the last 16 by Norway this summer.
Even those closest to him do not know how disappointed he was to miss out, given that playing for Brazil at a World Cup had long been one of his biggest dreams.
"When Joao Pedro is angry, he doesn't shout, he goes quiet," Junqueira said of his general personality.
After Chelsea 's struggles season and the lack of World Cup involvement, he had two weeks completely off.
Joao Pedro spent the rest of his summer in Rio training with Goncalves, his personal fitness coach since childhood, surrounded by friends and following many of the same routines he always has.
Ultimately, according to Goncalves, the frontman remains the same person, but one intent on becoming a truly "elite".
Since returning to Chelsea in the summer, he has scored eight goals in seven pre-season matches before finding the net 31 seconds into the new campaign at Fulham .
It now appears Joao Pedro may be the one capable of finally ending talk and concern of the club's number nine curse.

articles.title: Liverpool's midfield is fragile - but will they act in the transfer window?
articles.summary: Liverpool's draw at Newcastle emphasised once again their midfield fragility but will they act in the market and bring in a defensive-minded player?
articles.body:
A little over four minutes had passed at St James' Park on Sunday and Liverpool had started encouragingly, keeping the ball well and with urgency in their play.

Ryan Gravenberch created space with a brilliant touch to get past Lewis Miley but instead of shooting from the edge of the box or playing Dominik Szoboszlai through, the Netherlands international lost possession.

Just 11 seconds later, Newcastle were ahead through Anthony Elanga after a devastating counter that required one pass after Amar Dedic's initial clearance.

Liverpool simply had no structure when out of possession. It was schoolboy stuff and a nightmare start for Andoni Iraola.

It was a similar story in the second half when Gravenberch was dispossessed after trying a back heel on the edge of the Newcastle box.

This time, Yoane Wissa went on a brilliant run through the centre - evading an array of Liverpool players - and played the ball to Joe Willock, who finished in style.

As Iraola alluded to after, perhaps one of his players should have had the know how to commit a foul in that situation but Liverpool were punished again.

Looking back on both goals, Gravenberch's decision-making should have been better and perhaps the centre-back pairing of Virgil van Dijk and Jeremy Jacquet could have engaged quicker rather than holding off.

But having a defensive midfielder stationed accordingly would, in all likelihood, have nullified the threat.

Liverpool have not had an out-and-out number six since Fabinho, who left in 2023 , and as it stands Iraola's preference is a two-man pivot in midfield with Florian Wirtz playing as a number 10.

Both of those two midfielders, Gravenberch and Szoboszlai, were in the Newcastle box when Liverpool lost possession before Elanga's opener.

If Liverpool are to be taken seriously, they simply cannot concede goals like that regularly.

Iraola tends to avoid major debriefs in the dressing room after a game, with his personal preference to speak to the players a day later.

Asked in his post-match news conference about what could be done to prevent the kind of goals his side conceded, the Liverpool head coach suggested that it was not due to the type or identity of midfielders he had selected.

"I think it's just not personnel," said Iraola. "I understand you are telling me basically that Ryan Gravenberch is the six and he is on the edge of the box - but if he shoots and he scores we are saying what a play from Ryan Gravenberch."

It was an interesting point, given that Gravenberch produced the assist for Cody Gakpo's equaliser.

But shortly after Newcastle went 2-1 up, Iraola reacted by bringing on Alexis Mac Allister for Wirtz and Liverpool did seem more stable defensively - even if the Argentina international prefers to play as an eight.

Szoboszlai made zero tackles and won three of his 10 duels (30%) while Gravenberch similarly failed to make a tackle and won four of his 10 duels (40%).

When Mac Allister came on, he made two tackles and won four of his five duels (80%).

"We have to adapt as a team to these situations and we have to know that these situations can happen," added Iraola.

"I think the second goal, we probably did better in terms of having the numbers to defend - we don't make the foul, or go to the first challenge or probably reduce the distance with the ball carrier, so it's an incredible goal.

"Situations [are] just not because one person is playing there, [it] is something that we have to correct between a lot of players."

At full-time, the xG was 1.43 to Newcastle and 2.73 to Liverpool - indicating Newcastle had ruthlessly seized their opportunities against Iraola's side.

Will Liverpool act before the window ends?

On Sky Sports, former Liverpool striker Daniel Sturridge did not hold back in his criticism.

" Liverpool do not have that profile of player right now." said Sturridge. "The team has needed a defensive midfielder for three years. If you analyse the midfield, they are all naturally attacking players."

At Liverpool , the focus in the remaining days of the transfer window is clear. Their stance is unchanged in that the priority remains wide attacking players rather than midfield, even after the exit of Curtis Jones.

As always, if an opportunity presents itself in the market then Liverpool will consider it but Iraola is understood to be satisfied with his depth in midfield - with Wataru Endo, Trey Nyoni and James McConnell as the back-up options.

Liverpool have previously enquired about Adam Wharton but Crystal Palace 's stance is that the 22-year-old is not for sale.

Under Jurgen Klopp, Liverpool tried to get Moises Caicedo in 2023 and when Arne Slot arrived in 2024, Liverpool were keen on signing Martin Zubimendi from Real Sociedad.

But that fell through when the now- Arsenal midfielder turned the move down.

Gravenberch had a brilliant season under Slot as Liverpool cruised their way to the Premier League title, perhaps masking the issues temporarily by covering over emerging cracks.

Liverpool 's summer window 12 months ago then became about super-charging their attack with Alexander Isak, Florian Wirtz and Hugo Ekitike, rather than reinforcing the middle of the pitch.

Those fault lines are much clearer now and Iraola will know that his midfield must become harder to break down or else his side will keep on conceding.

As Iraola alluded to after, perhaps one of his players should have had the know how to commit a foul in that situation but Liverpool were punished again.

Looking back on both goals, Gravenberch's decision-making should have been better and perhaps the centre-back pairing of Virgil van Dijk and Jeremy Jacquet could have engaged quicker rather than holding off.
But having a defensive midfielder stationed accordingly would, in all likelihood, have nullified the threat.
Liverpool have not had an out-and-out number six since Fabinho, who left in 2023 , and as it stands Iraola's preference is a two-man pivot in midfield with Florian Wirtz playing as a number 10.
Both of those two midfielders, Gravenberch and Szoboszlai, were in the Newcastle box when Liverpool lost possession before Elanga's opener.

"I think it's just not personnel," said Iraola. "I understand you are telling me basically that Ryan Gravenberch is the six and he is on the edge of the box - but if he shoots and he scores we are saying what a play from Ryan Gravenberch."

Szoboszlai made zero tackles and won three of his 10 duels (30%) while Gravenberch similarly failed to make a tackle and won four of his 10 duels (40%).
When Mac Allister came on, he made two tackles and won four of his five duels (80%).
"We have to adapt as a team to these situations and we have to know that these situations can happen," added Iraola.

"I think the second goal, we probably did better in terms of having the numbers to defend - we don't make the foul, or go to the first challenge or probably reduce the distance with the ball carrier, so it's an incredible goal.

At full-time, the xG was 1.43 to Newcastle and 2.73 to Liverpool - indicating Newcastle had ruthlessly seized their opportunities against Iraola's side.
Will Liverpool act before the window ends?
On Sky Sports, former Liverpool striker Daniel Sturridge did not hold back in his criticism.

" Liverpool do not have that profile of player right now." said Sturridge. "The team has needed a defensive midfielder for three years. If you analyse the midfield, they are all naturally attacking players."

At Liverpool , the focus in the remaining days of the transfer window is clear. Their stance is unchanged in that the priority remains wide attacking players rather than midfield, even after the exit of Curtis Jones.

As always, if an opportunity presents itself in the market then Liverpool will consider it but Iraola is understood to be satisfied with his depth in midfield - with Wataru Endo, Trey Nyoni and James McConnell as the back-up options.
Liverpool have previously enquired about Adam Wharton but Crystal Palace 's stance is that the 22-year-old is not for sale.
Under Jurgen Klopp, Liverpool tried to get Moises Caicedo in 2023 and when Arne Slot arrived in 2024, Liverpool were keen on signing Martin Zubimendi from Real Sociedad.
But that fell through when the now- Arsenal midfielder turned the move down.
Gravenberch had a brilliant season under Slot as Liverpool cruised their way to the Premier League title, perhaps masking the issues temporarily by covering over emerging cracks.
Liverpool 's summer window 12 months ago then became about super-charging their attack with Alexander Isak, Florian Wirtz and Hugo Ekitike, rather than reinforcing the middle of the pitch.
Those fault lines are much clearer now and Iraola will know that his midfield must become harder to break down or else his side will keep on conceding.

articles.title: Real Madrid vs Real Sociedad: Mbappé-Vinicius, una sociedad por explotar
articles.standfirst: Su conexión directa aparece en 19 goles de los 269 goles desde que comparten equipo
articles.summary: Su conexión directa aparece en 19 goles de los 269 goles desde que comparten equipo
articles.body: Son las dos grandes estrellas del Real Madrid. Los dos máximos referentes de un equipo que exhibe músculo en ataque. Y, también, una sociedad que, después de dos temporadas, no ha encontrado la química que haga del peligro individual un temor colectivo. Es una de las misiones en las que Mou tiene terreno para mejorar respecto a lo logrado por Ancelotti, Xabi Alonso y Arbeloa. Hace algo más de dos años, el 14 de agosto de 2024, Vinicius y Mbappé jugaban por primera vez juntos. Fue en Varsovia, en la Supercopa de Europa que los blancos ganaron a la Atalanta, y el primer gol del francés vestido de blanco. Desde entonces, el Madrid ha jugado 125 partidos, 89 con ellos en el campo. De los 192 goles marcados cuando los dos han jugado, solo 19 (9,8%) han llegado a través de su conexión directa. Una cifra que sorprende por lo baja que es. El total de goles marcados por el Madrid desde que juegan juntos es de 269. La primera vez que el Madrid llegó al gol al juntarse Vinicius y Mbappé fue en su quinto partido juntos, el 1 de septiembre de 2024. Ante el Betis, en Chamartín, el delantero francés hizo los dos goles. El segundo, desde el punto de penalti, después de un derribo en el área al brasileño. Fue la primera de las diez interacciones entre ellos que acabaron en gol con Ancelotti. De ellas, ocho tuvieron el camino de acción de Vini culminada por Mbappé. Tres fueron ante el Barcelona (Supercopa y Montjuïc), pero sin poder evitar la derrota (5-2 y 4-3). La temporada pasada, marcada por las convulsiones en la Casa Blanca, la producción directa de goles creados de manera directa entre Vinicius y Mbappé se redujo a nueve, uno menos que la anterior. Seis fueron durante la breve etapa de Xabi Alonso (Oviedo, Espanyol, Villarreal, dos goles en Atenas ante Olympiakos y Girona). Bajo el mando de Arbeloa fueron tres, todas en Champions: Mónaco, Benfica y Bayern. En el Allianz, el 15 de abril, el 2-3 llegó de un pase de Vinicius a Mbappé. La dirección de las acciones previas de gol de la temporada pasada fue de 7-2 a favor del brasileño. De las 15 conexiones con gol nacidas de Vinicius hacia Mbappé, tres son con un penalti al brasileño La puesta en escena oficial del Madrid 2026-27, el del regreso de Mourinho, fue con otro partido sin goles creados entre Vinicius y Mbappé. El partido de ambos fue grisáceo. Vini, al margen de la batalla que mantuvo con sus marcadores y la grada, apenas fue capaz de generar las acciones de desequilibrio que son el ADN de su juego. Su talento se ahogó en la trama defensiva montada por Manolo González y los suyos. Mbappé sí escapó de esa tela de araña, pero mostró una versión que nada tuvo que ver con lo visto en el Mundial y la Bota de Oro que ganó gracias a sus 10 goles. Una cifra no vista desde 1970, con Gerd Müller. En la casa del Espanyol, Mbappé mostró una de sus caras más erráticas. Diez disparos, de ellos tres entre los tres palos, no le sirvieron para abrir su cuenta de goles en busca de su tercer Pichichi en España y el noveno seguido en su carrera. En manos de Mourinho queda que el brillo de sus dos estandartes del equipo pase de lo individual a lo colectivo. En lo primero, los dos ya han demostrado que son capaces de hacerlo de manera potente. Lo segundo es una tarea pendiente que necesita grandes títulos. Hasta ahora, el Madrid de Vinicius y Mbappé suma una Supercopa de Europa y una Intercontinental. Piezas de caza menor para la camiseta que defienden y el potencial que ellos tienen.

articles.title: The Hoddle of Coffee: Tottenham Hotspur News and Links for Wednesday, August 26
articles.summary: Good morning everyone – September is right around the corner and you know what that means: It’s time for the US Open! This year’s edition will not feature me...
articles.body:
September is right around the corner and you know what that means: It's time for the US Open!

This year's edition will not feature men's World No. 1 Jannik Sinner, marking the third straight major where either he or Carlos Alcaraz are missing. But this isn't about singles.

This is about the mixed doubles event. The US Open experimented with a new mixed doubles format last year. Instead of a real tournament, they're making this more of an exhibition-style tournament in the lead-up to the actual thing.

It was a shame because that meant fewer opportunities for actual doubles players, whose spots were taken by superstarts on the singles circuit. The good news is doubles specialists won last year.

This year's event probably features an even more stacked cast, featuring Alcaraz on the same team with Serena Williams. Don't get your hopes up for them, though. Alcaraz is a terrible doubles player, and Serena has understandably looked a little out of depth since returning to the tour this summer. Could still be fun for them.

Defending champions Sara Errani and Andrea Vavassori

Alexandra Eala and Felix Auger-Aliassime

I think the silliest thing is that the actual doubles players will need to get through qualifying to play the actual tournament, which should tell you I'm not the biggest fan of this event. That's because I'm one of those lame tennis purists. But I am open to change! However, the new tournament should never be used in any sort of metrics when determining titles, win percentages or any other success on the tour. Because all this is just a glorified exhibition.

But I'm giving it a chance, I say to myself.

Fitzie's track of the day: Tomorrow is Forever, by Dolly Parton

Dan KP ($$) : "Tottenham's Premier League-centric recruitment policy still comes with risk"

BBC : "All the best Savinho – welcome Savio… new club, new name for Spurs signing"

The Guardian : "De Zerbi hopes Sávio's fresh start will help Spurs' much-needed rebrand"

articles.title: SV 07 Elversberg 2026/27 season preview: Transfers, pre-season, predicted lineup & predictions
articles.summary: Not to everyone’s delight, Elversberg are active in the transfer market ahead of their first-ever top-flight season. The smallest town to be represented in B...
articles.body:
Not to everyone's delight, Elversberg are active in the transfer market ahead of their first-ever top-flight season. The smallest town to be represented in Bundesliga is backed by investor Frank Holzer, who is the head of pharmaceutical company Ursapharm, which didn't go well with the traditional ethos of German football.

After missing out on a promotion the previous season with a narrow defeat to Heidenheim in the playoff, Elversberg faced a similar scare in the final month of the 2. Bundesliga campaign. A defeat to eventually relegated Fortuna Düsseldorf made them wait until the final matchday of the season to write history.

The club from a town of 13,000 inhabitants has only made the jump to the second division in 2023. Despite the promising 2024/25 campaign, few predicted them to be around the top once again since their long-serving coach Horst Steffen was poached by Werder Bremen , while top scorers Fisnik Asllani and Muhammed Damar returned to their parent club Hoffenheim .

And, in the middle of the season, 12-goal hero Younes Ebnoutalib joined Eintracht Frankfurt . To their credit, Vincent Wagner's side maintained their momentum after the departure of the Moroccan attacker with David Mokwa proving to be the perfect replacement.

Their form at the Ursapharm-Arena an der Kaiserlinde was a big factor as Hertha and Schalke were the only teams to return home with three points. In the end, Elversberg followed the latter to win automatic promotion to Bundesliga .

A goal-scoring center-back in his playing career, Vincent Wagner wasn't able to go beyond Regionalliga. However, he has now become a Bundesliga head coach at the young age of 40.

After Asllani and Damar's memorable loan spells, Elversberg glanced at Hoffenheim once again to replace Steffen. Including three years in Sinsheim, Wagner worked with youth teams in four different clubs.

The Nordhausen native has managed back-to-back promotions, leading Hoffenheim II to 3. Liga before joining Elversberg. His repertoire of working with youth teams perfectly suits Elversberg's policy in the transfer market.

Christian Weber, who signed Christos Tzolis during his time at Fortuna Düsseldorf, is preparing a Bundesliga squad for the first time. Weber and co. are tasked with finding promising youngsters so that debutants Elversberg could emulate Heidenheim's success instead of an immediate relegation like Holstein Kiel.

Bambasé Conté and Jarzinho Malanga returned to their parent clubs after playing their part in the promotion season, while Die Elv hope to reach an agreement with HSV for the permanent transfer of Immanuel Pherai as they did for fellow midfielder Lukasz Poreba .

With Cole Campbell ( Dortmund ) and Maurice Krattenmacher ( Bayern ), Elversberg signed prospects from Germany's big clubs. The club shattered its transfer record for the US youth international as they parted ways with €6 million to sign the winger who only played 90 minutes of Bundesliga football for BVB and Hoffenheim last term.

According to Transfermarkt, they also spent €2.5 million to secure loan deals for Noel Futkeu (Frankfurt), Francis Onyeka (Leverkusen) and Noah Darvich ( Stuttgart ). The former finished as top scorer in 2. Bundesliga last season despite his club Greuther Fürth needing a playoff tie to stay in the division.

articles.title: Who is Dev Chaudhary? The son of a businessman who's getting flak for amateur batting in DPL 2026
articles.summary: Explore who Dev Chaudhary is, his cricket background, and why the New Delhi Tigers opener is facing heavy online scrutiny over his criticism in DPL 2026.
articles.body:
Dev Chaudhary has become one of the most talked-about names in this year's Delhi Premier League, though not for the reasons any young cricketer would hope for.

His position at the top of New Delhi Tigers' batting order has come under the scanner following a duck against South Delhi Superstarz on August 16.

Cricket fans have focussed heavily on Chaudhary's experience, his technique, and the decision to trust him with a powerplay opening role in a high-profile city tournament.

MAKE YOUR BET WITH DAFABET AND GET UP TO 200% WELCOME BONUS

His batting stance has drawn particular attention, with some comparing elements of it to former Australia captain Steve Smith, another player known for an unorthodox setup at the crease.

But unlike Smith, whose unconventional style is backed by years of elite performance, critics have questioned whether Chaudhary has shown enough at the senior level to justify opening the innings in a tournament of this profile.

According to a report in Free Press Journal , a DDCA trial document from 2021 lists him as an Under-19 all-rounder who specialises in middle-order batting and right-arm fast bowling.

However, those roles look quite different from the opening batter position he now occupies for New Delhi Tigers. That document, however, doesn't establish any real senior-level competitive history, which has only fuelled further questions about how he ended up in this spot.

@93Yorker shared a video and wrote: "This fraud Dev Chaudhary can't even hold bat properly but he is still playing in Delhi premier league 😭🤣 - look at the non striker reaction 😂😭."

Some fans have gone further, alleging political connections or family wealth played a role in his selection.

@CricketElysium wrote, "He Is Dev Chaudhry son of a big businessman in Delhi. Just look at his running and catching technique here. He doesn't even seem to know how to run properly, yet he is selected and playing in the Delhi Premier League. Meanwhile, so many genuinely talented players go to waste simply because they never get the opportunities they deserve."

User @Vipintiwari952 raised similar doubts, pointing to the lack of a clear domestic playing history. "Is there a fraud going on in the Delhi Premier League? Meet Dev Chaudhary, born 14 May 2004. He barely looks like he can hold a bat, it looks like school-kid batting. No proper stance, can't bat, but still comes in the top order. He doesn't seem to have played any proper domestic cricket. There is just an old DDCA U-19 trial document that lists a Dev Chaudhary as an all-rounder. So if he hasn't played domestic cricket, how is he featuring in the DPL?"

Interestingly, not all the backlash has been aimed squarely at Chaudhary himself. Cricket handle @MentionCricket noted that questions were also raised over how he made it into the DPL despite reportedly not appearing in the DDCA T20 League.

He wrote: "Questions raised over Dev Chaudhary's selection in the Delhi Premier League. His batting performance against a left-arm spinner, including five consecutive defensive dot balls in the powerplay, has sparked debate over whether he was ready for the level.

"Questions were also raised over how he reached the DPL despite his name reportedly not appearing in the DDCA T20 League, 40-over league or auction list. However, the criticism was directed at the selection process, not the player himself. The mistake lies with the selectors and the team for handing out chances at such a major platform."

Journalist @captainshanky echoed a similar sentiment, writing, "Cases like Dev Chaudhry are exactly why I'm not a big fan of these state-run T20 leagues. Sure, they've opened avenues for some talented players to make a mark in the IPL, but there's so much muck that needs cleaning."

How has Dev Chaudhary responded to the criticism?

When asked directly about the controversy surrounding his selection, Chaudhary declined to engage with the question, simply saying, "I want to skip the question."

He was more forthcoming, though, when asked about his unusual batting technique, and defended his natural style in an interview with Unfiltered Cricket Launda.

"It doesn't matter how you hold the bat; I've always held it the way I do, and it has always worked for me," he said.

articles.title: Celtic captain slams ‘scared’ team-mates for humiliating Champions League collapse
articles.summary: Celtic were 4-0 up on aggregate against LASK but went on to lose 5-1 to shockingly miss out on Champions League qualification
articles.body:
Celtic captain Callum McGregor accepted there were no excuses for the players after their incredible Champions League play-off collapse .

McGregor put his team 4-0 up on aggregate against LASK when he struck from 18 yards in the 21st minute in Austria but they went on to lose 5-1 on the night after extra time.

Defeat sends Celtic into the Europa League and delivers a damaging financial blow that will cost the club at least £20million.

"We got what we deserved," McGregor told Amazon Prime. "I thought we were so passive. All night. We actually looked scared to go and win the game, and when you are 3-0 up it's psychological.

"To be honest I didn't think we were that good in the first leg either. We scored at good times and kind of got away with it. You go 3-0 and you think you've got a real chance but when you play like that you can't have any excuse whatsoever.

"We have to suck it up, apologise to the supporters and the club because there is no way that we should lose that game.

"We've got to stick together, we've got to suck it up, and now you'll see what kind of characters are in there."

McGregor admitted there was a "nervousness" about Celtic due to what was at stake but the 33-year-old added: "When you play like that and you're so passive and you go 1-0 up in the game and it still doesn't settle you, then you can't have any excuse, and that's on us."

Defeat is the latest in a string of Champions League qualifying failures and Celtic's slow start to the transfer window will again come under scrutiny.

When asked if it could be levelled that the squad was not ready or strong enough this time, McGregor paused and said: "I guess not, no. Everyone's happy for two or three weeks and then you fall at a big hurdle, these questions are going to get asked.

"It's as much on the players as anything else to be honest. You can't lose that game by such a big margin and then start looking for excuses elsewhere. We have to accept that."

Martin O'Neill admitted the defeat ranked as one of his most painful nights as Celtic manager.

"I would say absolutely, yes," he said. "I'd put it down before the disappointment of losing the Uefa Cup final in 2003, but it's so, so disappointing.

"We should have been out of sight by half-time. We scored a goal, which was great, we missed two great, great opportunities. And then we give them a lifeline just before half-time and then one just after it. And they come roaring back.

"And obviously we conceded, from our viewpoint, not good goals at all. But that's my team and that's my responsibility.

"I'm disappointed that we've conceded the goals in the manner which we did."

When asked whether his squad was strong enough, O'Neill said: "These are tough games. And it might only be a Champions League qualifying game, but it felt like a Champions League game. I thought they were a fine side.

"But that doesn't matter. We should have been able to have seen it through. And we didn't do. Talking about the squad, that's for another day."

articles.title: When is the Carabao Cup third-round draw? Date, start time and how to watch
articles.summary: Everything you need to know about the draw for the next round of the League Cup
articles.body:
The draw for the Carabao Cup third round takes place this week as more teams from the Premier League , including current cup winners Manchester City , enter the competition and learn who they will face.

Most top-flight clubs, such as Chelsea and Tottenham , entered the tournament in the second round with those who are competing in European competitions this season now involved as well.

Arsenal , Liverpool and Manchester United are among those to enter at this stage.

Their participation also means that the third round will be played across two midweeks in order for the teams involved in the Champions League, Europa League and Conference League to juggle their match schedules.

Here's everything you need to know about the draw:

When is the Carabao Cup third round draw?

The draw for the Carabao Cup third round will take place on Wednesday 26 August . It will follow the conclusion of the second round tie between Preston and Everton which kicks off at 8pm BST, meaning the draw could start at around 10.15pm BST .

Before the main draw, there is a pre-draw to decide if the eight Champions League and Europa League clubs will be at home or away. This part is before Preston North End's Round Two tie against Everton on Sky Sports.

The main draw will take place following the conclusion of Round Two tie, the first eight ties will involve those Champions League and Europa League clubs. Their home or away position will have already having been decided. They will then be drawn against a team in a separate bowl with the remaining teams in the competition – so cannot meet one another at this stage.

Following the conclusion of those eight ties being drawn, the final eight ties will be drawn as normal.

From Round Three onwards, there is no longer a divide between the Northern and Southern sections.

The Carabao Cup third-round draw will be shown live on Sky Sports Main Event and Sky Sports Football following the conclusion of Preston v Everton.

Sky Sports subscribers will also be able to watch the draw live online via the Sky Go app.

32 teams are involved in the draw including 23 winners of second round ties and nine additional Premier League clubs who are also competing in European competitions this season.

Those teams in Europe and entering the competition for the first time this season are: Arsenal , Aston Villa , Bournemouth , Brighton & Hove Albion , Crystal Palace , Liverpool, Manchester City , Manchester United and Sunderland .

Of those, Brighton can be in Europe through the Conference League, but that competition does not begin until October, so it does not affect the Round Three schedule.

The ball numbers will be confirmed on this morning ahead of the draw.

When will the Carabao Cup third round be played?

The third round of the Carabao Cup is scheduled to take place across consecutive weeks, starting on 7 September and 14 September. The ties will be played midweek as single-leg fixtures with the winners progressing to the fourth round.

articles.title: Newcastle predicted XI vs West Brom: Woltemade set to start as Magpies rotate for EFL Cup
articles.summary: Newcastle United welcome West Bromwich Albion to St James’ Park on Wednesday night looking to book their place in the third round of the EFL Cup.The Geordies...
articles.body:
Newcastle United welcome West Bromwich Albion to St James' Park on Wednesday night looking to book their place in the third round of the EFL Cup.

The Geordies opened their Premier League campaign with an encouraging 2-2 draw.

However, the focus now switches to a competition Newcastle have taken seriously in recent seasons.

The Magpies lifted the EFL Cup in 2025 and have reached the quarter-finals in each of the last four campaigns.

New Newcastle boss Matthias Jaissle will be keen to keep that record intact.

There were plenty of doubts surrounding Newcastle heading into the new season after a summer of major change.

However, their performance at the weekend against Liverpool offered plenty of encouragement.

The Magpies led twice and were unfortunate to surrender three points via a stoppage-time penalty, with Jaissle impressed by the fight and energy shown by his young squad.

The Baggies have won all three of their competitive fixtures this season, scoring nine goals in the process.

Their latest victory was a 3-1 comeback against recently relegated Burnley , with Isaac Price scoring twice.

James Morrison's side also beat Rotherham United 4-1 in the first round of this competition and will arrive on Tyneside believing they can cause another upset.

But Newcastle have a strong record against the Baggies, winning seven of their last 14 meetings and four of their last six at St James' Park.

Jaissle is expected to make several changes as Newcastle prepare for a tough Premier League fixture on Saturday.

Tino Livramento and Joelinton remain sidelined, while Dan Burn is also unavailable after suffering ankle ligament damage.

William Osula should be fit despite picking up a knock against Liverpool, but Nick Woltemade , 24, is expected to replace him at the top of the attack.

Joe Willock could be rewarded with a starting berth after scoring off the bench in the league opener.

New signings Aladji Bamba (£35 million) and Bazoumana Toure (£42m) are both expected to make their full debuts.

Ewen Jaouen; Leo Shahar , Malick Thiaw , Fabian Schar , Lewis Hall ; Aladji Bamba, Joe Willock; Jacob Murphy , Bazoumana Toure; Yoane Wissa , Nick Woltemade.

The Magpies led twice and were unfortunate to surrender three points via a stoppage-time penalty, with Jaissle impressed by the fight and energy shown by his young squad.
The Baggies have won all three of their competitive fixtures this season, scoring nine goals in the process.
Their latest victory was a 3-1 comeback against recently relegated Burnley , with Isaac Price scoring twice.
James Morrison's side also beat Rotherham United 4-1 in the first round of this competition and will arrive on Tyneside believing they can cause another upset.
But Newcastle have a strong record against the Baggies, winning seven of their last 14 meetings and four of their last six at St James' Park.
Jaissle is expected to make several changes as Newcastle prepare for a tough Premier League fixture on Saturday.
Tino Livramento and Joelinton remain sidelined, while Dan Burn is also unavailable after suffering ankle ligament damage.
William Osula should be fit despite picking up a knock against Liverpool, but Nick Woltemade , 24, is expected to replace him at the top of the attack.
Joe Willock could be rewarded with a starting berth after scoring off the bench in the league opener.
New signings Aladji Bamba (£35 million) and Bazoumana Toure (£42m) are both expected to make their full debuts.

articles.title: Barcelona will not force exit-linked defender out despite growing Manchester United interest
articles.summary: Alejandro Balde’s future at Barcelona may have become one of the more unexpected talking points of the summer, but the club has no intention of pushing the l...
articles.body:
Alejandro Balde 's future at Barcelona may have become one of the more unexpected talking points of the summer, but the club has no intention of pushing the left-back towards the exit door.

According to Mundo Deportivo (h/t FCB World ), Barcelona will not force Balde to leave despite the strong message recently delivered by Hansi Flick .

The defender's omission from the squad for the match against Elche , coupled with Xavi Espart being selected to start, has intensified speculation surrounding his situation.

Yet, for all the uncertainty surrounding his role, Balde remains focused on staying and fighting for his place in the Barcelona starting XI.

Barcelona leave the final decision to the player

Barcelona's position is clear: Balde will only be allowed to leave if he personally decides that he wants a new challenge and is able to bring an attractive offer to the club.

The Blaugrana are not seeking to move him on or attempting to convince him to accept a transfer. Instead, the final decision over his future is expected to rest largely with the player himself.

Barcelona will not force Balde to leave. (Photo by Daniela Porcelli/Getty Images)

Balde, for his part, is not currently considering an exit . His intention is to remain at Barcelona and work towards regaining his place in the starting line-up.

A departure would only become a realistic possibility if the club were to directly inform him that he is no longer part of their plans.

Until that happens, the defender appears prepared to continue competing for his position.

Balde's situation has changed considerably over the past few days.

Until recently, despite regular transfer rumours and reported interest from Manchester United , Balde's future appeared to be tied to Barcelona.

That was also the player's preference. He had continued to ignore the speculation surrounding a possible departure and was willing to accept that his role could be different this season.

Manchester United are showing serious interested in Balde. (Photo by Yasser Bakhsh/Getty Images)

Balde knew that a starting place would no longer be guaranteed, but he was prepared to compete for his opportunities under Flick.

However, Flick's decision to leave the 22-year-old out of the squad entirely sent a clear message and added further intrigue to the situation.

Despite the recent developments, there is no indication that Barcelona are preparing to close the door on Balde or force a transfer through.

Flick's message may have made the defender's situation more complicated, but Balde still intends to respond on the pitch.

At this stage, he wants to earn his way back into the manager's plans rather than look for an immediate escape route.

articles.title: The pressure and the problem behind Liverpool’s transfer puzzle
articles.summary: ANALYSIS: Reinforcements are needed if Andoni Iraola’s football is to be a success at Anfield – but, Miguel Delaney explains, choosing where to invest is not...
articles.body:
Liverpool have a customary management meeting at the start of September, just after the transfer window closes, and the tone of it is currently subject to one main aim.

The football hierarchy, led by Richard Hughes, know the squad just has to be bigger. It's an absolute priority, with a week of the window remaining, and there's a pressure. Within that, though, there's also a problem.

There are multiple areas to focus on, without that much money to spend. This is a strangely thin and lopsided squad. As one source says, "it's like they're in a boat with six different leaks but which one do you plug?" If they spend the available budget in one or two areas, they're short in another.

That is potentially compounded by the way that Andoni Iraola plays. While Liverpool are most obviously shallow at full-back and central midfield, the Basque manager's ideal football is so intense that you really need proper back-up in every outfield position to apply it to its maximum. Otherwise, necessary overuse can bring injury.

Liverpool consequently have to bolster so many areas, but would have to get very creative to do them all. In other words, they're going to have to choose.

And that certainly isn't from the notionally strategic targeting of stars that we saw last summer.

The fact that Newcastle United were the first opposition, with Alexander Isak a central dramatic figure but a fringe performer in that 2-2 draw, only emphasises a contrast that many in the market have been commenting on.

This time last year, Liverpool were the picture of largesse, with industry figures talking about how they were taking an entire project - and an idea - to "maturation".

They were gearing up to pay a record Premier League fee for Isak, at £125m, having already spent almost £200m on attackers. More than that, they were apparently "zagging" when everyone was "zigging"; exactly the kind of counter-intuitive approach that keeps you on top; opting for individual quality when other teams were going for team control.

It's instead incredible how quickly they've fallen behind, while supposed maturation has just seen the squad seem smaller in size.

This consequently looks set to be a frantic final week, where Liverpool just can't be as calculated as last year.

Many might quip that could be a good thing, given the knock-on effects of last summer's window - and how they've even played into this market's difficulties - are still being felt.

Such circumstances have nevertheless raised surprise that Liverpool have been so intent on Paris Saint-Germain's Bradley Barcola , given that the Qatari-owned project want well in excess of £110m. It was that price which put Arsenal off.

Such a deal could be offset by the sale of Cody Gakpo , in one of many situations in this market that almost resembles a housing-market chain. Manchester City remain interested.

The focus on a winger also points to just how much Iraola's own coaching prioritises attack, especially for how the "chaos" that creates can tilt the tactical shape of an entire match. Put simply, if you are forcing the opposition to constantly think about your attack, they can't put your defence under the same pressure. It's Liverpool going with it, embracing the rock and roll again.

For all the reservations, this is exactly what they appointed Iraola for.

Others would now take a more conservative view, and point to how the set-up threatens to repeatedly leave Iraola's side susceptible to the kind of breakaways that Newcastle United enjoyed on Sunday.

Reflecting some of the wider issues, however, Liverpool do actually have a top target for defensive midfield.

Multiple sources say that is Iraola's hinge player at Bournemouth , Alex Scott .

A complication is that they can't currently pay the kind of fee that even make the south-coast club consider a sale, estimated at around £90m. As such, there's a sense that Liverpool will wait until next year, and make do in the way that Arne Slot did in 2024-25. Ryan Gravenberch may become newly important again.

There is a risk to that, if it's Scott they absolutely want, since Chelsea are one of many clubs extremely keen on the 23-year-old. Bournemouth have so far warned off all suitors, insisting they won't even entertain bids in this window, but Chelsea are considering whether to test that with a high offer.

At the least, Iraola has proven he is a coach who is very good at making do. He doesn't publicly complain, and has repeatedly shown a willingness to tactically compromise.

It's why so many executives have been describing him as a "dream appointment" in the modern environment, that is so dominated by directors and executives.

Duly, Hughes and the Liverpool hierarchy are arguably coming under much greater pressure than the coach.

There's still a difference between tactically compromising for an upwardly mobile mid-table side like Bournemouth, and doing it for Liverpool. The demands are bigger, the needs are greater.

Right now, Liverpool arguably need around six players, for a best-case scenario. The current thinking from various sources is that they'll end up with a net addition of two, potentially meaning three incomings and one sale.

There's a hope that would be enough to make "a huge difference". Otherwise, in the words of one source, "there's going to be a lot of concerned faces" at that September meeting.

articles.title: Freixa: "El homenaje a los campeones del mundo en el Camp Nou debe cancelarse"
articles.standfirst: El ex directivo del Barça considera que no debe producirse por la "vomitiva y cobarde actuación del dispositivo policial en Elche"
articles.summary: El ex directivo del Barça considera que no debe producirse por la "vomitiva y cobarde actuación del dispositivo policial en Elche"
articles.body: La carga policial el pasado domingo en Elche sigue dando que hablar. Las imágenes de aficionados del Barça portando esteladas y enfrentándose a la policía se hicieron virales y el club azulgrana condenó los hechos por lo que consideró una actuación policial desmesurada. En las imágenes se podía ver cómo un aficionado del Barça se enfrentaba a la policía queriendo agredirles y, una vez neutralizado, un agente le golpea cuando está ya inmovilizado. Estos hechos han causado indignación en el club y también en el ámbito político y social. El último en dar su opinión ha sido Toni Freixa, ex directivo del equipo barcelonista, que no dudó en tomar medidas desde el club. "No tengo ninguna duda de que el homenaje a los campeones del mundo en el Spotify Camp Nou debe cancelarse. Y no por la vomitiva y cobarde actuación del dispositivo policial en Elche, que también", decía Freixa en sus redes sociales. Y continuaba. "Sino sobre todo por la lamentable reacción de las instituciones del Estado ante el episodio. La catalanofobia les hace cerrar filas. Cerrémoslas nosotros también", comentaba el ex directivo en relación al primer partido liguero que se jugará en el feudo azulgrana este jueves ante el Athletic Club.

articles.title: Real Madrid’s new signing finally set for first start in Real Sociedad clash – report
articles.summary: Real Madrid are expected to give Marc Cucurella his first start at the Santiago Bernabeu on Wednesday, with the summer signing in line to be the only alterat...
articles.body:
Real Madrid are expected to give Marc Cucurella his first start at the Santiago Bernabeu on Wednesday, with the summer signing in line to be the only alteration to Jose Mourinho's starting XI against Real Sociedad .

According to AS , Mourinho is not planning a major overhaul for Real Madrid's first home match of the 2026/27 La Liga season.

Instead, the Portuguese coach is expected to keep faith with a side close to his strongest available lineup, with Cucurella's introduction at left-back standing out as the key change.

The match could therefore offer the Bernabeu faithful their first proper look at one of the club's notable summer arrivals from the opening whistle.

Cucurella has already had his first taste of action in a Real Madrid shirt, coming off the bench against Espanyol , but Wednesday's clash against Real Sociedad is expected to mark his first start.

Cucurella is set to start against Real Sociedad. (Photo by Christof Koepsel/Getty Images)

The Spaniard was signed before the World Cup and now looks ready to take a more prominent role in Mourinho's plans.

AS reports that the left-back is expected to be introduced into an otherwise largely unchanged team.

With another La Liga fixture against Malaga coming up next Sunday, Mourinho may opt to make further adjustments later in the week.

For the visit of Real Sociedad, though, the priority appears to be continuity rather than rotation.

Santiago Bernabeu to honour World Cup champions

Cucurella's first start will come on a special occasion for the player following his success with the Spanish national team at the World Cup.

Mourinho will not make many changes to his starting XI vs Sociedad. (Photo by Christof Koepsel/Getty Images)

As reported before, Real Madrid are planning to pay tribute to the left-back at the Santiago Bernabeu, recognising his role in Spain's triumph.

Cucurella was an important figure throughout the tournament and started every match as the national team lifted the trophy.

The occasion will also have significance for Real Sociedad captain Mikel Oyarzabal , who will return to Madrid as a World Cup champion and is also expected to receive recognition.

For Cucurella, though, the evening could bring a different kind of milestone.

The defender will have the opportunity to combine a celebration of his international success with his first start for one of the biggest clubs in world football.
